reviewContext.userProblem: Three riela issues are still open. (1) #32: riela session resume/rerun and workflow run --resume hydrate the entire persisted store (every CLI record, message and canonical snapshot, plus a second full loadAll in FailClosedSQLiteWorkflowRuntimeStore.hydrate) before the first JSONL event. On a large store this stalls for minutes. (2) #27: graceful cancellation is persisted as failed with failureKind cancelled. Agent-gateway turns cancelled by the host surface as providerError, invalid output or adapterFailure. Sessions whose runner was hard-killed stay running forever. (3) #74: there is no first-class way for an LLM brain node to generate a workflow, have the runtime validate and run it as a bounded child session, and get its result back.
requiredOutcomes: #32: resume, rerun and --resume hydrate only the target's session family (same root_session_id plus the target). Identity high-water marks stay metadata-only. A synthetic 200-session large-payload regression seeds in under 5 s and emits the first JSONL record within 5 s. The root cause is documented.

#27 P1: WorkflowSessionStatus and WorkflowStepExecutionStatus gain a persisted 'cancelled' case with tolerant decode (unknown → failed). Graceful cancellation persists status cancelled with failureKind cancelled. Every terminal predicate treats cancelled as terminal. Exit code stays 1, and cancelled is not resumable but can be rerun.
#27 P2: agent-gateway turns and executeWithRetry rethrow CancellationError when the host task is cancelled, never providerError or policy errors. Deadline expiry still reports timeout.

#27 P4: riela session reconcile (dry run by default, --apply) marks running sessions whose per-session flock can be acquired as cancelled with a stable 'runner process lost' reason, and never modifies live sessions. blocksResume and the FailClosed terminal hook handle cancelled. A docs file describes what is done and the follow-ups.

#74: authored transition.dynamicWorkflow is validated by DefaultWorkflowValidator. DynamicWorkflowPolicy enforces deny-by-default privileges, size bounds and a key allowlist on the brain envelope. The runner materializes a generated workflow through the shared TemporaryWorkflowPayload materializer, validates it, runs it as a child session with parent/root lineage and generatedWorkflow provenance (iteration, digest), delivers one dynamicWorkflowResult message, and repeats until finish or maxIterations (budgetExceeded). Durable resume and invalid-iteration recovery never re-run the brain.

#74 example: examples/brain-generated-workflow-loop validates cleanly and completes two distinct generate/execute iterations under riela workflow run --mock-scenario. It is registered in the catalog (expectedMockScenarioCount 45) and has user docs.
swift build succeeds and swiftlint reports no new warnings in changed files.

designDecisionsAndRationale: #32 hydrates the session family rather than only the target, because nested resume re-enters reserved children (user-QA 1). It uses the existing idx_workflow_runtime_snapshots_root through a new SessionFamily extension file, so SQLiteWorkflowRuntimePersistenceStore.swift stays owned by ISW2-27a.

#27 makes cancelled a real persisted status picked up by the generated session_status column, and keeps failureKind cancelled. isCancellation lets legacy failed+cancelled rows behave the same (user-QA 3, 6).
#27 orphan detection reuses the per-session execution flock, which the kernel releases on process death. The lock is held across the re-read and save to avoid a resume race (user-QA 5).

#74 is a runner-level transition extension rather than a builtin add-on, so it reuses cross-workflow nested reservation, publication hooks and recovery. The policy checker reads the raw envelope JSON because Codable drops unknown keys (user-QA 7, 8).

A single prepareDynamicIteration helper (overBudget/invalid/valid) is shared by the pre-commit hook, post-commit dispatch and resume recovery, so iteration gating, validation, stamping and digest stay deterministic across resume (RV-74c-1, RV-74c-2).

Operator amendment (2026-10-24, after the blocked-only wave 1 of session-1): plans run strictly serially 27a → 32 → 27b → 74a → 27c → 74b → 74c → 74d to avoid shared-tree compile breakage. This order is a superset of every shared-file ordering above. ISW2-27a also owns TaskDispatch+Handover.swift and WorkStoreTakeoverTests.swift. Workers continue from the existing uncommitted session-1 work in the tree.

Checkpoint amendment round 1 (2026-10-24, dispatch-plans comm-000043, reason integration-paths-outside-writePaths): the integration finding ISW2-27a-INT-RETENTION-CANCELLED showed TerminalRetentionPlan.make protects every family containing a 'cancelled' session because its terminal set is the string literal ["completed", "failed"]. ISW2-27a now also owns Sources/RielaCore/TerminalRetentionPlan.swift, Tests/RielaCoreTests/TerminalRetentionPlanTests.swift and Tests/RielaCoreTests/WorkflowRerunInputCarryoverTests.swift (already modified by 27a work). No other plan, ordering or design decision changes.
intentionalTradeoffs: Between waves 1 and 2, the FailClosed terminal hook skips cancelled sessions until ISW2-27c lands item 8a.
Only the confirmed O(store) hydration is removed for #32; the low-CPU stall cause stays unreproduced (user-QA 2).
Unknown persisted status strings decode as failed and the raw string is not preserved (user-QA 6).
Reconcile marks orphans cancelled rather than adding a new abandoned status; network-filesystem stores are unsupported.
Invalid generated definitions and child failures return to the brain (onFailure return) and count toward maxIterations (user-QA 9).
Add-on names in dynamicWorkflow.allow are checked only for shape if no add-on registry is reachable from RielaCore.
supportedEdgeCases: A CLI-only resume target with no canonical row is seeded as a family of one.
A canonical-only reserved child snapshot rooted at the target is hydrated.
Legacy failed+cancelled rows satisfy isCancellation; a cancelled cross-workflow child, fanout branch or nested child terminal is recorded as terminal.
A rerun from a cancelled source and importAcceptedHistory from a cancelled source both succeed.
Reconcile handles a canonical-only running snapshot, a tombstoned id (retired), a --session id that is not running (notRunning), and a session that changes during reconcile (skipped).
A vendor stopReason cancelled without host cancellation keeps existing behaviour; a timeout racing cancellation reports timeout only when the deadline expired.
A dynamic transition selected for the (maxIterations+1)th time fails with budgetExceeded before any reservation, in both the durable hook and post-commit dispatch.
A crash after reservation and before delivery, or after the parent commit and before an invalid result append, resumes with exactly one result message and no brain re-run.
Under simulatesCrossWorkflowDispatch the dynamic child still really runs through the scenario adapter.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Sessions whose lock lives on a network filesystem.
Detached execution surviving a short-lived driver (P5).
Generated workflows calling registered workflows or nesting dynamic calls (rejected by policy).
Unowned suites that fail because of new behaviour; these are reported as dependency objects.

Candidates come from scalar SQL only (never loadAll) over running CLI records and canonical snapshots. The verdicts are orphaned, live, retired, skipped and notRunning, using one SessionExecutionLockRegistry per sweep with a release in a defer.

--apply holds the lock across the re-read and the save, and marks orphans cancelled/cancelled with the reason 'runner process lost; reconciled by riela session reconcile', cancelling their running executions. Live sessions stay byte-identical, and a dry run writes nothing.
